json.title: KEPCO switches on a 345 kV substation for the Saemangeum data center cluster
json.summary:
KEPCO has energized a new 345 kV substation that serves the Saemangeum data center cluster, adding 1 GW of connection capacity for early tenants.

The utility cautioned that it can take on few further interconnection requests until transmission upgrades along the west coast corridor are finished. The source names neither the tenants nor the number of pending requests, and gives no completion date for the upgrades, which are widely expected to finish in 2027.
json.why_it_matters: Saemangeum is one of the few data center locations outside the capital region with grid capacity actually in hand. For hyperscale buyers facing closed connection queues elsewhere in Korea, 1 GW of available capacity widens the realistic siting options, but anything beyond it waits on transmission work.
json.expert_lens: Energizing the substation is a starting point, not an answer. The source does not say how the 1 GW is split among the first tenants or how much remains, so later entrants need to confirm available capacity directly. If the corridor upgrades are the bottleneck, connection dates follow KEPCO's transmission investment schedule, and lease contracts should carry that into their ready-for-service terms. The next signal is progress on the west coast upgrades and whether KEPCO reopens interconnection requests.
